newsitem.title: USA: Demand for Asarco copper continues strong.
newsitem.headline: Demand for Asarco copper continues strong.

text.p: Asarco Inc operations are performing well and demand from its customers for copper continues strong, chief executive Richard de J. Osborne said Thursday.

The company reported net earnings of $40.6 million, or $0.95 per share, for the first quarter compared with $35.7 million, or $0.84 per share, a year earlier when profit included an after-tax gain of $7.2 million from the sale of an interest in one of the company's mining properties.
Sales of products and services were $715.6 million compared with $735.0 million in the first quarter of 1996.
Commenting on the outlook for the balance of 1997, Osborne said, "The fundamentals of the metal markets, particularly in the case of copper are quite good.

"Over the last nine weeks, supplies of copper in terminal market warehouses have declined over 50,000 tons. Total inventories of copper, including producer and consumer stocks, are at historically low levels and demand from our customers for copper continues to be strong.
"We believe that consumption will exceed supply throughout the rest of 1997 and in 1998.
"The company's operations are performing well and together with the favorable market outlook we believe the company should continue to perform well."

Osborne pointed out "Asarco's earnings improved in the first quarter of 1997 despite lower copper prices. Net earnings, excluding the non-recurring gain in 1996, increased 42 percent over the comparable quarter of 1996."

He said the first quarter profit increase is principally the result of lower costs at the company's domestic copper operations, gains from its price protection program, reduced interest expense and a reduction in its effective tax rate.

Asarco said its beneficial interest in mined copper production declined 7 percent in the first quarter of 1997 to 233.5 million pounds, however, beneficial sales of copper in were about the same as in the prior year.

It said the decline in mined copper production was primarily due to the partial curtailment of the Hayden concentrator at the Ray mine which began in October 1996. Full operations of the concentrator will be resumed in early May.
Asarco said the period of reduced operations and sales of copper concentrates in the first quarter of 1997 allowed the company to reduce its concentrate inventory.
First quarter 1997 earnings include pre-tax gains of $16.0 million ($10.4 million after-tax) from the company's price protection program, Asarco said.

The gains resulted from the sale of put options in 1996 covering copper sold in the first quarter of 1997, gains from the sale or exercise of call options in the first quarter of 1997, and adjustments to the carrying value of call options which were marked to market at the end of the first quarter.
At March 31, 1997, the company had synthetic put options covering 42.6 million pounds of copper and call options covering 88.1 million pounds of copper to be sold over the balance of 1997.
In the first quarter of 1997, the Government of Peru approved a reinvestment allowance for Southern Peru Copper Corp's program to expand the Cuajone mine.

The reinvestment allowance provides Southern Peru with tax incentives in Peru and, as a result, certain U.S. tax credit carryforwards for which no benefit has previously been recorded are expected to be realized, thereby reducing Asarco's effective tax rate for 1997. The estimated effect of the reduction in the effective tax rate for the first quarter of 1997 is $2.5 million.
